comments.note: In ledger-store.test.ts, the archiveDocuments beforeEach/afterEach performs a manual readdir+rm loop to clean up files written to store.planPath. This is slightly fragile — if a future test writes subdirectories to planPath the loop will fail silently (rm with { force: true } on a directory without { recursive: true } does nothing). A simpler cleanup would be rm(store.planPath, { recursive: true, force: true }) followed by mkdir(store.planPath) in the next test's beforeEach; this mirrors the pattern already used for tempLedgerRoot.

The archiveDocuments tests use repeated await (await import('fs/promises')) inline calls instead of adding the needed fs/promises symbols to the top-level import statement (which already imports mkdtemp, rm, readFile). This was a pragmatic choice to avoid touching the outer import, but it slightly inconsistent with the existing test style. A clean follow-up would consolidate: add writeFile and mkdir to the top-level import.

comments.note: archiveDocuments() catch block catches all Error types (not just ENOENT). A storageDir permissions failure or disk-full condition would be silently swallowed and the filename added to skipped[] with no distinction from a missing-source skip. For production hardening consider differentiating ENOENT (source not found) from other I/O errors and rethrowing non-ENOENT errors.

comments.note: ledger-store.ts archiveDocuments(): the console.error message reads 'Archive skipped (source not found)' but the catch block catches ALL errors — not just ENOENT. If copyFile fails due to a destination-side error (storageDir missing, permission denied, disk full), the log message actively misleads callers into thinking the source file was absent. Non-blocking for this scope (existing AC only require the skip behavior, and QA confirmed acceptable), but the message should be updated to something like 'Archive skipped (copy failed)' or differentiate ENOENT vs other errors.

ledger-store.ts archiveDocuments(): no path-traversal guard on filenames. If a caller passes '../../../etc/passwd' the join(planPath, filename) will resolve outside planPath. This is documented by QA as 'callers must sanitize', which is acceptable for an internal method. A one-liner defensive check `if (path.basename(fn) !== fn) { skipped.push(fn); continue; }` would harden the method for free with no behavioral changes for valid inputs.

ledger-store.test.ts archiveDocuments tests: the 'copy succeeds' test does not spy on console.error for the non-ENOENT path, and the 'source missing' test does not assert that console.error was called with the expected message. Adding a vi.spyOn(console, 'error') assertion would lock in the observable side-effect contract. Non-blocking — functional correctness is fully covered.
